newsitem.title: DJIBOUTI: Jailed Djibouti politicians' court appeal fails.
newsitem.headline: Jailed Djibouti politicians' court appeal fails.

text.p: Djibouti's Supreme Court on Sunday dismissed an appeal by five local politicians, including three former ministers, jailed for six months for insulting the head of state.

Moumin Bahdon Farah, a former justice minister, Ahmed Boulaleh Barreh, a former defence minister, and Ali Mahamade Houmed, a former industry minister, and two other members of the ruling Popular Progress party (RPP) were sentenced last August.
They were also ordered to forfeit their civic rights for five years, after being found guilty of accusing President Hassan Gouled Aptidon of "ruling by terror and violating the constitution".
On Sunday the Supreme Court rejected their plea after their lawyer had declared: "There is no rule of law in Djibouti." When the verdict was announced, Barreh shouted: "There is no justice."
